title.en: Axisymmetric coil Green geometry and elliptic modulus

summary: Compute the source-offset radius, elliptic modulus squared, and distance used by the filament-coil Green expression.

capability: Axisymmetric coil Green geometry and elliptic modulus
Compute the source-offset radius, elliptic modulus squared and distance used by the filament-coil Green expression.
operation: observation point and coil centres -> regularized radius, modulus squared and distance
discovery.model: Scalar observation geometry for aligned circular coils.
discovery.geometry: One observation point paired with one-dimensional coil-centre arrays.
discovery.boundary: Raw observation radius must be nonnegative; underflow, overflow and nonfinite geometry raise ValueError.

identity.direction: observation point and coil centers to regularized Green geometry
identity.definition: Apply the fixed 1e-8 m observation-radius offset and compute m and the distance denominator elementwise.
identity.model: Scalar observation geometry for aligned circular coils.
identity.geometry: One observation point paired with one-dimensional coil-center arrays.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; modulus squared dimensionless.
identity.boundary: Raw observation radius must be nonnegative; underflow, overflow, and nonfinite geometry raise ValueError.
assumptions: All coil vectors have one-dimensional matching shapes.
The offset is applied exactly once before the response operator.

inputs.name: observation_radius_m
inputs.description: Raw cylindrical radius of the observation point.
inputs.constraints: Finite; must be nonnegative (a raw radius in (-1e-8, 0) is rejected: the axis offset would silently regularize it to a positive one -- declared hardening); the regularized radius must be finite and positive.

inputs.name: observation_z_m
inputs.description: Axial coordinate of the observation point.

inputs.name: coil_radius_m
inputs.constraints: Finite 1-D with strictly positive entries, same shape as coil_z_m.

outputs.name: regularized_radius_m
outputs.description: Observation radius after the axis offset, the value the filament-coil Green operators must receive.
outputs.constraints: Finite and positive; paired once with the response operator (which does not offset again).

outputs.name: modulus_squared
outputs.description: Per-coil squared elliptic modulus m = k^2.
outputs.constraints: Finite values in (0, 1] on accepted non-singular geometry; overflow from finite but extreme inputs raises ValueError (declared hardening).

outputs.name: distance_m
outputs.description: Per-coil Green geometric distance denominator sqrt((r0+rl)^2+(z0-zl)^2).

preconditions: All coil vectors have one-dimensional matching shapes.
supported: Finite paired coil arrays, the axis offset, endpoint modulus values, and declared overflow/underflow failures.
excluded: Coil-field evaluation, singular response handling, and arbitrary overflow behavior beyond the validated float64 domain.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for nonfinite, negative, mismatched, nonpositive-radius, underflowed, or overflowed geometry.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: No iterative runtime failure is defined; NumPy floating-point failures are converted to ValueError by validation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is direct geometry arithmetic.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No geometry tuple is returned after validation failure.

example.description: Compute regularized geometry for one observation point and two coils.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus
radius, modulus, distance = compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus(
    0.3, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]))
assert radius == 0.3 + 1e-8
assert np.all((modulus > 0.0) & (modulus <= 1.0))
assert np.all(distance > 0.0)
example.expected: The returned radius is 0.30000001 m; both modulus-squared values are in (0,1] and distances are positive.

scope: Source-regularized geometry quantities against an independent recomputation.
A finite extreme geometry with an underflowed modulus is rejected before the Green response.

Independent evidence (tests/field/test_coil_green_geometry_evidence.py): the modulus m = 4*R*a/((R+a)**2 + (Z-z0)**2), the distance squared and the complementary identity 1 - m = ((R-a)**2 + (Z-z0)**2)/D are recomputed in exact rational arithmetic from the same binary64 inputs and compared against the returned floats within their own rounding chains (8 eps for the modulus expression, 2 eps for the squared distance); m <= 1 with equality exactly on the ring follows from D - 4*R*a = (R-a)**2 + (Z-z0)**2 >= 0 and is asserted as an exact rational inequality.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to regularized modulus and distance geometry. Direct assertions in test_geometry_returns_source_regularized_radius_modulus_and_distance, test_geometry_rejects_invalid_inputs, test_negative_raw_radius_within_offset_width_is_rejected and test_geometry_rejects_underflowed_modulus_before_green_response in tests/field/test_filament_coil_green.py check the analytic geometry, raw-radius rejection and modulus-underflow boundary. That file is shared; its other field-response and elliptic-integral tests are not geometry-asset evidence. This does not establish coil-field evaluation, finite-wire physics or arbitrary-scale accuracy. C1 evidence adds an exact rational second source for every returned scalar, so the relation is decided without a floating-point re-derivation; the observed maximum relative deviation of the modulus is 1.87e-16, i.e. 0.84 eps, on the sampled table. It does not establish that this is the right observation geometry for a physical coil field; the Green kernel assets carry that, and their Biot-Savart evidence fixes the (2-m)K - 2E prefactor this modulus feeds.
known_limitations: No external cross-implementation comparison is bound to this contract; only the tests in this repository establish its behaviour.
Declared input hardening: raw observation radii in (-1e-8, 0) are rejected rather than silently regularized to positive values by the axis offset.

Declared output hardening: finite but extreme input magnitudes (e.g. r0 = rl = 1e308) that overflow the squared geometry sums are rejected with ValueError instead of handing a non-finite modulus or distance to the response operator.
A modulus of exactly 1 (observation point on a filament ring) is an admissible output; consumers must reject it (the response operator does).
The independent oracle recomputes the regularized geometry but does not bind an external code comparison.
A zero modulus caused by floating-point underflow is rejected here, an explicit boundary of this contract.

The exact rational comparison uses exactly representable radii and heights so that the recomputation is the exact value of the intended expression; arbitrary binary64 inputs would need the same analysis plus an input-rounding term.

The 8-eps modulus budget counts the eight roundings of the expression; an earlier draft stated eps/2 from a one-rounding assumption that does not match the chain, and that derivation was corrected before any code changed.

basis.statement: An exact rational second source decides every returned scalar, so the relation is decided without a floating-point re-derivation; the observed maximum relative deviation of the modulus is 1.87e-16 (0.84 eps) on the sampled table.
